description: Preprocess a weighted undirected graph so queries can test whether two vertices are connected using only edges strictly below a limit. Example 1: with edges 0-1 of weight 2 and 1-2 of weight 5, query(0,2,6) is true. Example 2: query(0,2,5) is false because the weight-5 edge is not strictly below the limit. Constraints: the graph has up to 10^5 vertices and edges, and paths are undirected.
intuition: A minimum spanning forest preserves the minimum possible bottleneck between every connected pair.

brute_force.approach: Run a limited-edge graph search for every query.

optimal.approach: Build a minimum spanning forest, preprocess binary-lifting ancestors with maximum edge weights, and test the path bottleneck.
optimal.time: construction O(m log m + n log n), query O(log n)

edge_cases: A vertex is connected to itself by an empty path.
An edge equal to the limit is not allowed in the path.
